definitions.explanation: A shop that sells souvenirs, local specialties, and gifts, typically found at tourist destinations, train stations, and airports.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{土産物屋|みやげものや}が{並|なら}んでいる。
examples.english: Souvenir shops line the area in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {観光地|かんこうち}の{土産物屋|みやげものや}で{友達|ともだち}にお{土産|みやげ}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought souvenirs for my friends at a gift shop in the tourist area.

examples.japanese: この{土産物屋|みやげものや}は{地元|じもと}の{名産品|めいさんひん}が{豊富|ほうふ}で、いつも{観光客|かんこうきゃく}でにぎわっている。
examples.english: This souvenir shop has a wide selection of local specialties and is always bustling with tourists.

notes:
A compound of {土産物|みやげもの} (souvenir goods) + {屋|や} (shop/seller). Typically found at {観光地|かんこうち} (tourist spots), {駅|えき} (stations), and {空港|くうこう} (airports).

FORMS:
- {土産物屋|みやげものや}: souvenir shop (standard)
- お{土産|みやげ}{屋|や}さん: souvenir shop (casual, polite)
- {土産|みやげ}{店|てん}: souvenir store (slightly formal)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土産物屋|みやげものや}で{買|か}う: to buy at a souvenir shop
- {土産物屋|みやげものや}が{並|なら}ぶ: souvenir shops lined up
- {土産物屋|みやげものや}を{覗|のぞ}く: to browse a souvenir shop

CULTURAL NOTE:
Buying お{土産|みやげ} (souvenirs) for family, friends, and coworkers is an important social custom in Japan. {土産物屋|みやげものや} at popular tourist destinations typically sell {名産品|めいさんひん} (local specialties) and {銘菓|めいか} (famous confections).
